slides.title: Our starting hypothesis, "keep C", survived four of five tests; the fifth showed that keeping C unchanged is not enough

claims.claim: Initial hypothesis, set before testing: retain C, because its low reported margin is an allocation effect rather than an avoidable economic cost
1. C earns more cash than its exit would save — Holds
evidence: $3.8M direct contribution against $0.4M avoidable fixed cost: exit gives up a net $3.4M a year before migration

claims.claim: 2. D cannot replace what C earns — Holds
evidence: Ceiling of 25% of C revenue = $1.5M (all of D's spare capacity) × 50% = $0.75M, against $3.4M at stake

claims.claim: 3. Exit costs and constraints bind — Holds
evidence: $2.1M first-year penalties against $0.9M approved cash; C in 9 of 14 major bundles; no substitute validated on every hospital model

claims.claim: 4. C is not driving customer attrition — Unproven
evidence: 9-percentage-point renewal gap is correlational and confounded (size, legacy equipment, coverage); no before/after evidence
Test 4 stays open, and the plan includes a way to resolve it (page 10)

claims.claim: 5. Retaining C as-is is acceptable — Fails: refine
evidence: Bundle fill 91% against 95% required; C faces price pressure; a $1.25M a year redesign saving costs $0.55M

claims.claim: Revised answer: keep C, but not unchanged. Fund the redesign, restore 95% bundle fill, use the renewals to open a consent-based path to D, and decide any 2029 sunset in Q4 2028 on observed evidence

slides.title: C's 8% margin is an allocation effect: only $0.4M of its $3.3M allocated cost is avoidable, against $3.8M of contribution

claims.claim: $3.4M a year of profit lost if C exits, before any migration: the decision-relevant figure, not 8%
evidence: Connector C walk, $M, FY2026: Sales 6; Direct variable cost 2.2; Avoidable fixed cost 0.4; Shared cost that stays (reallocated) 2.9; Reported profit 0.5
Direct contribution $3.8M = 63% of sales; reported profit $0.5M = 8.3%. Avoidable fixed cost $0.40M a year per Finance; variable cost fully avoidable

claims.claim: Two different margins
evidence: reported margin = (6.0 − 2.2 − 3.3) ÷ 6.0 = 8.3%; contribution margin = 3.8 ÷ 6.0 = 63.3%

claims.claim: 88% of the allocation stays
evidence: $2.9M of the $3.3M is shared regulatory documentation and plant depreciation, spread by historical engineering hours

claims.claim: The dashboard label misleads: "product gross margin" is measured after shared allocations, so it cannot rank products for an exit or capacity decision

slides.title: On contribution C is the strongest connector, 63% against D's 50%, and its exit would strand $2.9M of cost on A, B and D

claims.claim: On contribution margin C ranks first; on reported margin it ranks last
evidence: Reported margin (after allocations): A (sales $14.0M) 41.4%; B (sales $9.0M) 28.9%; C (sales $6.0M) 8.3%; D (sales $4.0M) 30%
Direct contribution margin: A 50%; B 42.2%; C 63.3%; D 50%
In dollars A's $7.0M contribution is largest; C's $3.8M equals B's

claims.claim: If C exits, the stranded cost lands on A, B and D, and B's reported margin falls to about 17%
evidence: Reported margin today vs after C exits: A 41.4% → 33.7%; B 28.9% → 16.8%; D (with 25% C migration) 30% → 22.3%
Pack gives no split of the stranded cost; assumed pro rata (1.2 : 1.2 : 0.8): A and B $1.20M → $2.29M each, D $0.80M → $1.53M. D includes $1.5M migrated revenue at 50%

claims.claim: The same margin-ranking logic would then pick B as the next "weakest" product, while total allocated cost falls by only $0.4M, from $6.5M to $6.1M

slides.title: Exiting C costs $4.75M of cash contribution in year one and $2.65M a year after, even if D wins the optimistic 25%

claims.claim: Every year: exit loses $2.65M even with D migration at its ceiling
evidence: C direct contribution lost −3.8; Avoidable fixed cost saved +0.4; D migration at ceiling (25% × $6.0M × 50%) +0.75; Recurring annual impact −2.65

claims.claim: Year one: one-time penalties deepen the loss to $4.75M
evidence: Recurring annual impact −2.65; First-year bundle penalties (one-time) −2.1; First-year impact −4.75
Penalty is first-year only, per Finance

claims.claim: Operating profit falls 26%, or 34% with no migration
evidence: Operating profit: Today (FY2026) 10.1; Exit C, 25% migration 7.45; Exit C, no migration 6.7
Operating profit = contribution 16.6 − fixed 6.5; exit: (16.6 − 3.8 + 0.75) − (6.5 − 0.4)

claims.claim: Penalties are one-time: even with every penalty waived, exit still loses $2.65M a year

25% of C revenue is a ceiling from three sales interviews, not a forecast; it needs customer-specific adapters and validation. Not yet costed: requalification, clinical documentation, lost A/B accounts

slides.title: No migration rate makes exit pay: even full migration to D still loses $0.4M a year, and D can absorb only 25% today

claims.claim: Recurring annual impact of exit, by share of C revenue migrating to D; impact = −3.8 + 0.4 + (share × $6.0M × 50%)
evidence: Shares above 25% are hypothetical: they exceed D's current capacity and would need new D capacity and a validated adapter at every account. Excludes the one-time $2.1M penalty

claims.claim: $6.8M of migrated D revenue needed to offset the $3.4M lost each year
evidence: $3.4M ÷ 50%: 113% of C's entire $6.0M revenue and 4.5 times D's spare capacity

claims.claim: Why D cannot close the gap: C's 63% contribution margin is higher than D's incremental 50%, so each dollar moved from C to D earns less
Migration crowds out D growth: the 25% ceiling would use all of D's $1.5M spare capacity, leaving no room for D's own organic growth
The 25% is unobserved: it is the portfolio team's ceiling from three interviews; Finance has not estimated any recapture beyond it

slides.title: With its penalty alone 2.3 times the cash envelope and C in 9 of 14 major bundles, a 2027 exit breaks board constraints

claims.claim: ≥95% bundle fill: fails
evidence: 9 of 14 major hospital relationships specify a bundle with C alongside A and B
No substitute for C has completed validation on every hospital model
Removing C leaves them incomplete; fill is already 91% and would worsen
−4 pp fill against the 95% minimum

claims.claim: ≤$0.9M one-time cash: fails
evidence: $2.1M of first-year penalties payable unless counterparties consent, at least $1.2M over the envelope
Replacement qualification and clinical documentation come on top
Those have not been costed yet
2.3x: $2.1M penalty ÷ $0.9M cash
Assumes the $2.1M penalty counts against the 2027 one-time cash envelope because it is a direct cash consequence of the portfolio change

claims.claim: Customer commitments: fails
evidence: Exit requires notice, replacement qualification and clinical documentation
Two bundle agreements are being renewed now
An exit notice would go into live negotiations
9 customers must consent

claims.claim: Cash contribution test: fails
evidence: Judged on cash, not the allocation report: contribution falls $3.4M a year before migration
It falls by $2.65M a year after the 25% migration ceiling
The $2.1M penalty comes on top in year one: −$4.75M

claims.claim: A 2027 exit needs the board to relax at least two of its own constraints; no other option does (page 12)

slides.title: Redeploying to D cannot replace C, because D's spare capacity caps the gain at $0.75M a year, available even if C stays

claims.claim: 4.5x: C's economics compared with the most D can add without new capacity
evidence: C profit lost on exit (contribution − avoidable fixed) 3.4; Most D can add at present capacity ($1.5M revenue × 50%) 0.75

claims.claim: Known: D has room for $1.5M more revenue whether or not C exits; migrating C customers would fill it and crowd out D's own growth
Known: the redesign needs one design team for about four months, then hands it back; not known: what those months cost, which we do not invent
Illustrative ceiling: a full four-month delay to D would cost at most 4/12 × $0.75M ≈ $0.25M, against $1.25M a year of savings
evidence: The $0.25M is a bound under a stated assumption, not an estimate of lost D sales

claims.claim: Redeploy to D? Yes, in sequence: C redesign March to June 2027, then D adapter validation and growth from July
D's 30% margin is after allocations; its 50% incremental contribution is still below C's 63%. D's growth adds value at the margin, not $3.8M of existing contribution

slides.title: The renewal gap does not show C causes churn: size, legacy equipment and coverage confound it, and it is untested

claims.claim: The claim: accounts that buy C renew less often, so C causes it
evidence: The CEO reads a scatter of hospital renewal rates by product mix as C causing dissatisfaction
9 pp lower renewal for C buyers

claims.claim: Correlation, not causation: C accounts differ systematically from the rest
evidence: No counterfactual: no before/after evidence that removing C raises retention
It cannot support exit, and it cannot rule out a C effect either

claims.claim: Three factors the comparison does not control for; each of these could lower renewal on its own
evidence: Smaller hospitals on legacy equipment (named in the briefing pack)
Lower customer-success coverage (named in the briefing pack)
Bundle fill of 91% at the nine C-bundle customers, caused by A/B misses: a further plausible confounder (our hypothesis, untested; the pack does not link it to renewals)

claims.claim: Tests to run before the Q4 2028 gate
evidence: Compare renewal within matched segments (size × equipment age × customer-success coverage)
Control for the bundle fill each account actually received
Code lost-account exit reasons for any mention of C
Track retention of any accounts that drop C or move to D

claims.claim: Only a gap that persists within segments feeds the sunset decision, valued against the $3.4M a year C contributes
evidence: Decision rule: within-segment gap

slides.title: The real service problem is bundle fill at 91% against a 95% contract, caused by A and B misses an exit would not fix

claims.claim: Fix the measure and the A/B misses, not C
evidence: C on-time fill (service dashboard) 98%; Contracted bundle fill (actual, nine bundle customers) 91%; Contract minimum 95%

claims.claim: The dashboard's 98% counts C as filled even when the bundle ships late because A or B is missing; the contract measures complete bundles
Redefine the KPI: bundle-level contracted fill becomes the headline service metric for every bundle customer; product-level fill only a diagnostic
Root-cause the A and B misses on the nine bundle accounts, size buffer stock or allocation priority, and report monthly to the board until fill holds at 95% or above for two consecutive quarters
Unknown: recovery speed. The pack gives no timeline or cost; Q3 2027 is a working target for Operations to confirm in February
The cause sits in A and B, not C: exiting C leaves the A/B misses in place and makes the nine C-bundles incomplete
evidence: Bundle fill is 4 percentage points below the contract minimum

slides.title: Only redesigning C adds value and meets every constraint, at +$2.4M over 2027–29 against −$8.7M for an immediate exit

claims.claim: Exit C in Q2 2027
evidence: Cash, 2027 −3.43; 2028 and 2029 each −2.65; Cumulative 2027–29 −$8.7M; −10.6 with no migration
One-time cash: ≥$2.1M penalties + qualification: fails
95% bundle fill: Worsens: no validated substitute
Customer commitments: Penalties unless 9 customers consent
Main risk: A/B bundle volume at risk (unquantified); B next "weakest"

claims.claim: Retain C unchanged
evidence: Cash 0 in all years
$0: meets
Needs A/B fix
Honoured

evidence: Cash 0 through 2029; −2.65 to −3.4 a year from 2030
$0 if exits match expiries: meets
Needs A/B fix; time to validate adapter
Honoured; exit only at expiry
Main risk: As retain; locks in high-cost C until 2029

claims.claim: Redesign C now, 2029 sunset gate
evidence: Cash, 2027 −0.13; 2028 and 2029 each +1.25; Cumulative $2.4M; +0.40 in the downside case
$0.55M + $0.35M reserve: meets
Needs A/B fix (in plan)

claims.claim: Exit effective 1 Jul 2027 (half-year loss plus full $2.1M penalty in 2027), 25% migration; redesign savings from 1 Sep 2027; downside on page 13

slides.title: The $0.55M redesign pays back in about 5 months and still breaks even if it delivers only a fifth of the $1.25M estimate

claims.claim: Redesign scenarios: cash contribution against retaining C unchanged, $M
evidence: Break-even: $0.24M a year from Sep 2027; $0.55M cost: −0.47; +0.24; +0.24; 0.00
Break-even with the full $0.9M spent: $0.39M a year: −0.77; +0.39; +0.39; 0.00

claims.claim: 5.3 months to pay back the redesign from run-rate savings
evidence: $0.55M ÷ $1.25M a year = 0.44 years

claims.claim: Breaks even at 19% of the estimated saving, or 31% if the full $0.9M is spent; the downside case still returns +$0.40M
The margin ranking goes away: if the saving comes out of direct cost, C's reported margin rises to about 29%, level with D's 30%
Operating profit rises 12%, from $10.1M to $11.35M a year at full run-rate
Caution: $1.25M equals 57% of C's $2.2M direct cost, an engineering estimate at current volume; the two-site pilot tests it before the whole line converts
Redesign cost excludes possible requalification tests at two customers; the downside case uses the $0.35M left in the envelope for them
evidence: Rounded. 2027 savings run Sep–Dec (4 months); the 2027–29 window is 2.33 years. Downside 2027: −0.90 + 0.63 × 1/12

slides.title: Use the two renewals to secure C supply, bundle-level service terms and a consent-based path to D, not to give exit notice

claims.claim: 1. The two bundle renewals: Renew with C, no exit notice; D + adapter substitution only with customer consent, after qualification; end terms with the 2029 cohort so any sunset is penalty-free
evidence: Commercial + Legal · Q1 2027; terms set at Feb board

claims.claim: 2. The other seven bundle customers: Confirm C supply through current terms; pre-notify the design change; agree requalification tests early with the two customers that need them
evidence: Account leads + Quality · Q1 2027

claims.claim: 3. Bundle service recovery: Bundle-level fill as the contract KPI on every dashboard; root-cause A/B misses; A/B buffer or priority for bundle accounts; monthly report until ≥95%
evidence: Operations · Start Feb 2027; target ≥95% by Q3 2027

claims.claim: 4. Penalty exposure: Carry the $2.1M as a contingent one-time liability tied to premature termination, not annual overhead (Finance's rule)
evidence: Finance · Ongoing

claims.claim: 5. D substitution evidence: Qualify adapter and quality with willing C customers; record actual acceptance, not interview estimates
evidence: Engineering (D) + Sales · From Jul 2027

claims.claim: Only consent or expiry makes a later exit penalty-free; fixing A/B fill protects all nine bundles
evidence: Why this order: the penalty stands unless counterparties consent; fixing A/B fill protects the nine bundles whatever happens to C

claims.claim: Leads and the Q3 2027 fill target are proposals for management to confirm; the briefing pack names neither owners nor a recovery date

slides.title: A staged plan with two gates protects $3.8M of contribution today and keeps a 2029 sunset open if the evidence turns

claims.claim: Gate 1, end Aug 2027 (convert the whole line?): go if the pilot run-rate saving is ≥$0.4M a year, the break-even with the full $0.9M spent, and no requalification failed; otherwise stop at the pilot sites, with spend capped inside the $0.9M envelope

Gate 2, Q4 2028 or the notice deadline (sunset in 2029?): only if the D adapter is validated on every hospital model in C bundles, acceptance is high enough, D capacity is in place, fill held ≥95% for 2 quarters, the renewal gap is causal and the exit bridge is positive
Plan by workstream, by quarter, 2027–29
evidence: C redesign: Design + validation; Pilot; Full line at run-rate savings (from Sep 2027)
Engineering team: On C; On D: adapter validation and D growth
Bundle fill: A/B root cause; recover to ≥95%; Sustain ≥95%; monthly board report
Contracts: Renew; 2 renewed; bundle terms run; requalification with 2 customers; 2029 expiries
D substitution evidence: Adapter qualification; observed acceptance; Only if Gate 2 passes: migrate at expiry

claims.claim: C contribution protected now, a year: $3.8M
Assumes redesign kick-off in Mar 2027, four-month validation and a two-month pilot. Contract notice periods are not in the briefing pack; Gate 2 must precede them

slides.title: None of the open unknowns is likely to flip the decision against exit, and each is tested at a gate in the plan

claims.claim: D substitution acceptance — Effect: None: even full migration of C revenue loses $0.4M a year
evidence: 25% is a ceiling from three sales interviews; adapters and validation are customer-specific
Resolved by: Observed acceptance in qualification (from Jul 2027)

claims.claim: Requalification at 2 customers — Effect: Low: the downside (3 months late, $0.9M spent, half the savings) is still +$0.40M
evidence: Not included in the $0.55M; could delay savings
Resolved by: Early engagement in Q1 2027; $0.35M reserve

claims.claim: Redesign savings at scale — Effect: Low: breaks even at 19% of the estimate (31% if the full $0.9M is spent)
evidence: $1.25M is an estimate at current volume, 57% of C's direct cost
Resolved by: Two-site pilot; Gate 1 threshold $0.4M a year

claims.claim: Speed of bundle-fill recovery — Effect: Same under every option, since the cause is A/B; matters for renewals
evidence: Fill is 91% against 95%; no recovery timeline or cost in the pack
Resolved by: Ops plan in February; monthly board tracking

claims.claim: Engineering opportunity cost — Effect: Low: illustrative ceiling ≈$0.25M against $1.25M a year of savings
evidence: Not quantified for the four months on C
Resolved by: Team moves to D from Jul 2027

claims.claim: C price pressure — Effect: Exit breaks even on run-rate only if C contribution falls about 70%, from $3.8M to $1.15M
evidence: Competitive pressure named, not quantified
Resolved by: Re-test C contribution at Gate 2
exit run-rate = −C contribution + 0.4 + 0.75 = 0, so C contribution = $1.15M

claims.claim: Key assumptions: FY2026 volumes and costs hold through 2029; the penalty is payable in full unless counterparties consent; the $0.4M avoidable fixed cost is Finance's estimate; cash effects are undiscounted (three-year horizon)

slides.title: Six decisions for the board keep $3.8M of contribution, avoid $2.1M of penalties and add about $1.25M a year

claims.claim: 1. Reject discontinuing connector C in 2027
evidence: Exit loses $4.75M in year one and $2.65M a year after
It breaches the cash and fill constraints

claims.claim: 2. Approve $0.55M for the C redesign, plus up to $0.35M reserve
evidence: Within the $0.9M envelope
Pilot at two sites first; Gate 1 at end of Aug 2027
About $1.25M a year of savings at run-rate

claims.claim: 3. Mandate bundle-level contracted fill as the service KPI
evidence: Operations to present an A/B recovery plan to reach ≥95%, with dates and cost

claims.claim: 4. Authorise renewal terms for the two bundle agreements
evidence: C retained; consent-based D substitution clause
Terms aligned to 2029 expiries

claims.claim: 5. Sequence engineering: C redesign Mar–Jun 2027, then D
evidence: The D adapter work also builds the evidence for any later sunset

claims.claim: 6. Set Gate 2 criteria for any 2029 sunset (Q4 2028)
evidence: Validated adapter, observed acceptance, sustained ≥95% fill
Causal renewal test and a positive exit bridge

claims.claim: $3.8M of direct contribution kept a year; $2.1M of first-year penalties avoided
